subject: LegacyBank - On-prem air-gapped deployment: hardware & offline ops follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: LegacyBank - On-prem air-gapped deployment: hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi Tom - great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call so your team has a single thread to track: 

Summary of customer constraints (as I heard them)
- Air-gapped environment (no outbound internet from inference cluster)
- Preference for on-prem Private deployment vs Hosted/Dedicated due to data residency and regulatory controls
- Existing DC has some NVIDIA capacity but procurement may buy dedicated nodes for this project
- Need clear offline installation and upgrade story for patches/OS and model updates

Questions we need you to confirm:
1) Is outbound traffic strictly prohibited for all maintenance (i.e., no periodic telemetry or egress to S3)?
2) Target latency and throughput SLAs (p95 latency and expected concurrent requests)?
3) Do you have a preferred vendor list or procurement constraints for hardware?
4) Do you plan to host key material in an HSM/KMS inside the air-gap, or will keys be managed separately?

What Redwood can provide now:
- On-prem installer image and air-gap install procedure (USB/ISO), with MD5 checksums and offline verification
- Hardware recommendation doc attached (redwood-onprem-hw-requirements.pdf) and a checklist for offline ops
- Work with your infra team to size GPU pools (we recommend X A100-40GB or Y 80GB equiv per 13B model serving tier - details in the PDF)
- Support for on-site enablement and an ops runbook for patching and model rollouts in offline environments

Proposed next steps
- Can we schedule a 60-min technical call next week between your infra team (network, security, procurement) and our infra lead Dev Patel to walk the hardware doc and offline install process?
- Please upload the current hardware inventory and network diagram (if possible) - you can attach to this thread.

Attached: redwood-onprem-hw-requirements.pdf (hardware guidance), template checklist

Thanks - I'll coordinate times once you confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0143

Subject: Re: LegacyBank - On-prem air-gapped deployment: hardware & offline ops follow-up

Marissa - thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers and a few details from our side: 

Answers
1) Correct - outbound traffic from the inference VLAN is not allowed. All maintenance must be possible via physically transported media or through our controlled jump-hosts.
2) Latency goal: p95 under 500ms for single-turn text generation (short prompts). Expected steady-state throughput: ~8 req/s; expected peak spikes up to ~30 req/s for short windows. Concurrency: roughly 20-30 concurrent sessions.
3) Procurement: we need vendor-neutral recommendations; Procurement requires a short vendor questionnaire. We can share the template.
4) Keys: we plan to use an HSM inside the data center for key material (no external KMS).

Current infra notes (attached)
- Inventory: a mix of Nvidia A100 (40GB) and a couple of older V100 racks (attached CSV).
- Network: segmented VLANs, dedicated storage with periodic allowed transfer via locked jump host (see network diagram attached).

Questions for Redwood
- Do you support an installer that can be deployed fully offline and validated without contacting Redwood cloud?
- How do you handle model updates and security patches in an air-gapped environment? Do you provide signed image bundles we can validate locally?
- Any minimum uptime/HA recommendations for the control plane in a fully private install?

I attached our HW inventory and network diagram. Happy to join a technical call next week; afternoons Pacific (Wed/Thu) look best.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior Director, Infrastructure
LegacyBank

Thanks Tom - this is very helpful. A few clarifications and immediate answers: 

Offline installer and signed bundles
- Yes: we support a fully offline installer (ISO/USB image) and provide signed model bundles and OS/manifests that your team can validate locally. We can provide SHA256 checksums and GPG signatures for all artifacts.

Model updates & patches
- Model updates: we support offline model bundle delivery. You can stage bundles on the internal artifact store and instruct the runtime to load them locally. We recommend a canary host pattern within the cluster for staged rollouts.
- Security patches: we provide periodic patch bundles; our recommended ops pattern is to apply OS/security patches during scheduled maintenance windows via USB or secure jump-host. Our on-prem runbook includes steps and rollback instructions.

Control plane HA
- For fully private deployments we recommend a 3-node control plane for HA, colocated in your management VLAN. The serving plane (GPUs) can be scaled independently. Details and example HA topology are in the attached PDF.

Hardware recommendation (high level)
- For 13B model serving with target latency and your peak profile: 2x A100-80GB equivalent per serving shard (can be 1x 80GB or 2x 40GB depending on batch/kv-cache config); cluster-level sizing depends on redundancy and expected concurrency.

Next steps
- Proposed tech call: Wed May 26, 10:00-11:00 PT (Dev Patel, me, your infra + security + procurement). Does that work?
- I'll also have our Implementation Engineer prepare the offline installer checklist and a draft vendor questionnaire answer set to speed procurement.

Fwd: I'm including a brief note from Dev below to address a couple of the specific offline ops questions.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Tom / Marissa - quick technical notes from the infra lead who would be on the call: 

Offline installation/validation
- We provide an offline installer (ISO) plus a signed artifact bundle for the runtime, model files, and supporting services. The process: bring ISO -> boot bootstrap host -> run installer -> follow manifest to place models and runtime. All artifacts are signed and verifiable via GPG/PKI.

Patch & model rollout pattern
- Patching: produce patch bundle -> sign -> transport via secure media -> stage to a staging host -> run smoke tests -> roll to production hosts using our local orchestration (zero-touch once staged).
- Model rollouts: we recommend staging on 1-2 nodes (canary), run perf tests and regression evals locally (we can provide the eval harness), then roll cluster-wide.

Hardware specifics (examples)
- 13B low-latency: recommend 2x A100-80GB per shard (or 4x A100-40GB depending on memory/kv-cache needs).
- If you will rely on older V100s: we can still run smaller models (7B) with quantization; performance will be lower and latency higher.

Security & HSM
- HSM integration is supported; we can integrate with on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11) for key unsealing. Keys are stored encrypted at rest and only unsealed by HSM at runtime.

Operational considerations
- If procurement chooses a vendor for bare-metal, please share AMI/firmware/BIOS baseline requirements - we will provide firmware/driver checks as part of the installer.

I'll come prepared with a short checklist and a reproducible offline install demo for the call.

- Dev
